Blank means exact match. Enter −1 or 1 for next smaller or next larger.

CGS 1060C · Microsoft Excel, Chapters 3–5
Chapter 3 · Entering functions
Three ways to enter a function
Function Arguments dialog
Formulas › Function Library › a category button (or Insert Function). One box per argument.
Bold argument names are required. The result previews at the lower left before you click OK.
Formula AutoComplete
Type = and the first letters. Double-click the function name (or press Tab).
A ScreenTip lists the arguments. Excel adds the closing parenthesis when you press Enter.
AutoSum arrow
Home › Editing › AutoSum arrow: Sum, Average, Count Numbers, Max, Min.
Guesses the adjacent range. Check the dashed border before pressing Enter.
SimNet mostly uses the dialog. In everyday work, AutoComplete is fastest, and it lists your named ranges too.

A blank cell means no data, so it's left out. A zero means the value was zero, so it counts.

Dates and times
TODAY and NOW update themselves
Entry
Stores
Shows (depends on format)
Changes
=TODAY()
46295
9/30/2026
whenever the workbook recalculates
=NOW()
46295.75
9/30/2026 18:00
whenever the workbook recalculates
Ctrl+; (typed)
46295
9/30/2026
never: it's a typed value
Neither function takes arguments, but the empty parentheses are required. The .75 in NOW is the time: three-quarters of a day is 6:00 PM.
Trap: Invoice dates, due dates, and signatures should be typed. TODAY() on an invoice changes every time someone opens it.
Hidden gem: =TODAY()-B4 gives days since the date in B4. Format the result as General or Number.

Text functions
Text functions build a new value in a new cell
A2 contains mARIA lopez. B2 is Maria, C2 is Lopez, and D2 is empty.
Formula
Result
=PROPER(A2)
Maria Lopez
=UPPER(A2)
MARIA LOPEZ
=LOWER(A2)
maria lopez
=LEN(A2)
11 (the space counts)
=CONCAT(B2," ",C2)
Maria Lopez
=TEXTJOIN(", ",TRUE,B2:D2)
Maria, Lopez (blank D2 skipped)
Trap: CONCAT adds no spaces. Give the space its own argument: " ".
Hidden gem: To replace the original text, copy the results and Paste Values over it (Chapter 2).

References to other sheets
Referencing other sheets: click, don't type
Reference
Means
=Jan!B34
cell B34 on the Jan sheet
='Sales Q1'!B4
sheet names with spaces get single quotes
=SUM(Jan:Mar!B34)
B34 on every sheet from Jan through Mar (3-D)
=[Budget.xlsx]Sheet1!A1
a cell in another workbook: creates a link
How: type =, click the other sheet's tab, click the cell, and press Enter while you're still on that sheet. Excel takes you back.
Hidden gem: A 3-D reference covers whatever sheets sit between the first and last tab. Drag a sheet outside that range and it drops out of the total.

Named ranges
Named ranges read like sentences and don't move
=Price*Tax_Rate
A name acts like an absolute reference: copy the formula and the name still points at the same cells.
Create
Select cells, type a name in the Name box, press Enter. Or Formulas › Create from Selection.
Use
Type it in a formula; AutoComplete lists names with a label icon.
Change
Formulas › Name Manager: edit Refers to, click the checkmark; or Edit to rename; Delete.
Naming rules
No spaces: use an underscore. Start with a letter or underscore.
It can't look like a cell address. TAX2024 is a cell (column TAX, row 2024), so Excel refuses it.
Create from Selection turns spaces in labels into underscores.
Trap: Delete a name that a formula uses and the formula shows #NAME?.

=IF(
Starts the function
D5>E5,
Logical_test: must be true or false
"Do not order",
Value_if_true

Value_if_false
Comparison operators:
=
<>
>
<
>=
<=
(<> means “not equal”)
Trap: Typed text needs quotation marks. The Function Arguments dialog adds them for you.
Trap: No commas inside numbers: =IF(B2>1,000,…) splits 1,000 into two arguments.

Financial function
PMT: make the time units match
=PMT(7%/12, 120, 250000)
→ ($2,902.71)
Rate
The interest rate per payment.
Monthly payments: annual rate ÷ 12
Nper
The total number of payments.
10 years of monthly payments: 120
Pv
The loan amount today.
Fv and Type are optional; leave them blank
Trap: Forget the /12 and the “monthly” payment comes out near $17,505: a yearly rate applied every month.
Why negative?: The result is negative because it's money going out. Use =-PMT(…) or a negative Pv to show it as positive.

Checking formulas
Error values tell you what went wrong
Shows
Means
Usual fix
#DIV/0!
dividing by zero or a blank cell
check the divisor
#N/A
a lookup found no match
check spelling, extra spaces, FALSE
#NAME?
Excel doesn't recognize a name
fix a typo, or add quotes around text
#REF!
a referenced cell was deleted
undo, or rebuild the reference
#VALUE!
wrong kind of data, like text in math
find the text cell
####
not an error: the column is too narrow
widen the column
A green triangle marks a possible problem, like a formula that skips an adjacent cell. Click the cell, then the Smart Tag, to see Excel's suggestion.

Chapter 4 · Grouping sheets
Grouped sheets: one edit lands on every sheet
Jan
Feb
Mar
Summary
Budget [Group]
Group
Shift-click the first and last tabs for neighbors; Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) to pick tabs one by one.
The title bar adds [Group]
Edit once
Typing, formatting, column widths, and headers and footers apply to the same cells on every grouped sheet.
Perfect for identical monthly sheets
Ungroup
Click a tab outside the group, or right-click a grouped tab › Ungroup Sheets.
If every sheet is grouped, use right-click
Trap: Forget to ungroup and your next edit quietly overwrites every sheet in the group. Look for [Group] before you type.

Fastest way

Rows and columns
Rows and columns: three habits
Insert whole rows
Home › Insert › Insert Sheet Rows keeps every column lined up. Inserting cells (last week) can shift one column out of step.
A new row appears above the selected cell
Double-click to autofit
Double-click a column's right border (a row's bottom border) to fit the contents. Fixes ####.
Format › Column Width sets an exact width
Unhide from both sides
Select the columns on both sides of the hidden one, then Format › Hide & Unhide › Unhide Columns.
The thin double line marks a hidden column
Trap: Hidden isn't secret. Anyone can unhide rows, columns, or sheets in two clicks.

Common confusion
Screen settings and paper settings are separate
On screen
On paper
Freeze Panes keeps headings visible while you scroll
Print Titles repeats heading rows on every printed page
Gridlines › View (on by default)
Gridlines › Print (off by default)
Headings › View: column letters and row numbers
Headings › Print
Zoom makes it bigger on screen
Scale to Fit: Width 1 page
Freezing panes does nothing to a printout. For headings on page 2, use Page Layout › Print Titles.
CGS 1060C · Microsoft Excel, Chapters 3–5
Demo in Excel: EX-04-17-PurchaseOrders-2024
Printing
Getting a sheet to print well, in order
1
Orientation: Landscape for a wide sheet (Page Layout › Orientation).
2
Scale to Fit: Width 1 page, Height Automatic.
3
Margins: Narrow if you need a little more room.
4
Print Titles: Rows to repeat at top: click the header row.
5
File › Print: check the preview, then choose Active Sheets, Entire Workbook, or Selection.
Trap: Width 1 page AND Height 1 page on a long list shrinks the text until no one can read it.
Remember: A print area from last week overrides everything. File › Print › Ignore Print Area bypasses it for one print.

Make it print right

Open a workbook with a long list. No file handy? Type Row in A1, =ROW() in A2, and fill down to A200.

Chapter 5 · Charts
Pick the chart that answers the question
Column or bar
Compares categories: which service sold most?
Use bar when category labels are long
Line
Shows change over time: how did sales move each month?
Include the dates or months when you select
Pie
Shows parts of one whole: what share came from each location?
One series, a handful of slices
Chart looks sideways? Chart Design › Switch Row/Column swaps what's on the x axis with what's in the legend.

Tables
A table knows where your data starts and ends
Grows by itself
Type in the next row or column and the table expands.
Fills formulas down
Enter a formula once; the whole column gets it (a calculated column).
Banding and filter buttons
Built in; turn them on or off in Table Style Options.
Headers stay visible
Scroll down and the headers replace the column letters.
=[@Qty]*[@Price]
A structured reference: “this row's Qty times this row's Price.” Name the table (Table Design › Table Name) and =SUM(Orders[Total]) works anywhere.

Demo in Excel: EX-05-12-PurchaseOrders-2024
Table tools
Total rows and Remove Duplicates: know what they do
Total Row
Table Design › Total Row. Each total cell has an arrow: Sum, Average, Count, Max, and more.
It uses SUBTOTAL, which counts only visible rows. Filter the table and the total changes to match.
Remove Duplicates
Table Design › Remove Duplicates deletes rows that match in every checked column.
Uncheck columns and more rows count as duplicates. Excel reports how many it removed.
Hidden gem: Check first with Highlight Cells Rules › Duplicate Values (last week), then decide what to delete.
Trap: Remove Duplicates deletes rows for good once you save. Work on a copy.
CGS 1060C · Microsoft Excel, Chapters 3–5
Demo in Excel: EX-05-16-PurchaseOrders-2024
Sorting and filtering
Sorting moves rows; filtering hides them
Sort
Click one cell in the column, then Data › A to Z or Z to A. Excel keeps each row together.
A to Z: text alphabetically, numbers smallest first, dates oldest first
Filter
Hides rows that don't match; nothing is deleted. Row numbers turn blue and skip.
Tables have filter buttons already; ranges need Sort & Filter › Filter. Data › Clear shows everything again.
Slicers
Clickable buttons that filter a table (or PivotTable). Table Design › Insert Slicer.
Multi-Select lets you pick more than one button
Trap: Select just one column and sort, and that column can separate from the rest of its rows. If Excel asks, choose Expand the selection.

What-if analysis
Goal Seek works backward; a data table tries many inputs
Goal Seek
You know the answer you want. Excel changes one input until the formula hits it.
What loan gives a $400 monthly payment? About $20,690.
Set cell must hold a formula. By changing cell must hold a typed value the formula uses.
Data table
Lists the formula's result for many inputs at once. $25,000 over 5 years at:
4%
$460.41
5%
$471.78
6%
$483.32
7%
$495.03
Two-variable tables vary a row input and a column input.
Both live at Data › Forecast › What-If Analysis.

CGS 1060C · Microsoft Excel, Chapters 3–5
Quick check
Type your answer in chat first, then I'll reveal it
1. COUNT or COUNTA: which one counts a column of names?
2. =VLOOKUP(E2,A2:C5,3) returns a wrong price and no error. What's missing?
3. You froze the top row, but page 2 of the printout has no headings. What do you need?
4. A table's Total row drops after you filter. Is that a bug?
COUNTA. COUNT only counts cells that contain numbers.
FALSE as the fourth argument. Without it, VLOOKUP accepts the closest match.
Print Titles (Page Layout). Freeze Panes only affects the screen.
No. The Total row uses SUBTOTAL, which includes only the visible rows.
